title: Lecture 6 — mutation, arrays, and pointers
summary: Trace references, shared objects and the difference between copying a reference and copying a value.
body:
Published slides verified on 17 November: arrays versus immutable lists, passing references into functions, aliases, addresses and dereferencing.

Updating an array element changes the shared object. Reassigning a variable changes the value held by that variable. With pointers enabled, &x obtains the address of x and *p reads through a pointer. These are distinct operations: sketch the storage locations and arrows before tracing them.

An array index can fail at runtime even when the program type-checks. Compare a reference copy with a fresh array construction, then explain which observations can change through aliases. The guide below develops the distinction.
